newsitem.title: USA: Donors to let US firms in on development projects.
newsitem.headline: Donors to let US firms in on development projects.

text.p: Donors to a World Bank trust fund to finance development in poor nations have tentatively agreed to open up $1 billion worth of projects for bidding by U.S. firms, Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin said on Wednesday.

That represents about one-third of the money in the one-year trust fund, which was set up as a stop-gap measure while the World Bank raised contributions from donors for its International Development Association (IDA) affiliate.

"While this result is not everything we wanted, we put enormous effort into this issue and, given the obstacles, I do believe this was the best we could achieve," Rubin said in a report to a House Appropriations subcommittee.

The donors had restricted U.S. companies from bidding on projects financed by the trust fund because Washington had not contributed to it. A final decision to lift the restriction will be made by the end of this year and is contingent on Washington coming up with its promised contribution to the IDA.
President Clinton is seeking Congressional approval for a $1.03 billion contribution to the IDA, including $234.5 million to clear U.S. arrears.
Congress last year approved $700 million for the IDA, but made release of the money contingent on Rubin's report.
